headline: KOSPI's 3.6% slide to 5,100 and a solid 10Y auction pull KTBs lower against a 5bp rise in the US 10Y: the KTB 10Y falls 2.0bp to 3.981% as foreigners buy 9,000 bond futures and the KTB–UST gap hits a new extreme
summary: KTBs reversed a weak morning and closed firmer with a long-end lead: the 3Y fell 1.6bp to 3.743% (59th percentile of its 1-year range), the 10Y 2.0bp to 3.981% (51st) and the 30Y 2.4bp to 4.050%, with the 20Y the best performer at −2.7bp; the 1Y was flat at 3.633% (90th) as the November 26 hike stays priced. 3s10s flattened 0.4bp to 23.8bp (2nd percentile) and 30s50s is −2.3bp. Bills stayed at 1-year highs (MSB 91-day 3.206%, CD up 1bp to 3.38%, CP 3.84%), so CP–CD eased to 46bp (91st). Spread products lagged the rally: the KDB 3Y fit widened 4.9bp to 18bp over KTB (42nd), AAA bank 1Y is 39bp (84th), AA- 3Y 67bp (68th) and KEPCO 3Y 41bp (80th).
drivers: KOSPI −3.6% turns bonds around after lunch

KOSPI opened up at 5,305, then slid to close −3.59% at 5,100.50 (low 5,069.83) as foreigners sold about KRW 1.4–1.7tn of stock; Samsung Electronics fell 4.5% and SK Hynix 7.9% ahead of Nvidia's first results since its CEO quit. The 3Y had been 0.8bp higher in the morning, so the swing into the close was about 2.5bp, all of it a domestic risk-off bid.
US Treasuries: a 5bp sell-off that KTBs ignored

The US 10Y rose 5bp to 5.15% on Nov 13 after October PPI (+0.3% m/m, 6.5% y/y, core +0.5%) kept a December Fed hike priced. At the 1-year beta of 0.47 that implied about +2.4bp for the KTB 10Y against an actual −2.0bp, so Treasuries explained none of the day and the local part was a 4.4bp rally. The KTB–UST 10Y gap widened to −117bp, again a 1-year extreme (0th percentile).

Foreigners bought 2,984 3Y and 5,999 10Y futures after selling 4,103 and 9,313 last week, so part of Friday's hedge selling was covered. KRX settles were not carried in the wraps we read; our basket fair values rose to 103.59 (3Y) and 108.36 (10Y, +18 ticks), so we cannot state the basis today.
10Y auction clears below market despite the dealer fines

The KRW 1.1tn 10Y main auction priced at 3.985% with a 304% bid-to-cover, and the KRW 1.1tn pre-sale for December 10 settlement at 3.940% (278%), the first 10Y sale since the Nov 11 collusion fines of KRW 1.63tn. Dealers cited lighter December supply ahead of the benchmark switch; USD/KRW was steady at 1,335.7.
data: Solid; supply worries after the fines eased.
−1.8% m/m (f n/a, p +1.9%); +13.5% y/y; export volumes +43.9% y/y, a record
Lower imported inflation, strong chip volumes.
Softer demand but no tail; 50Y beat 30Y.
Unanimous hold at 3.00%; a majority open to more tightening
view: Today was the mirror of Friday: the US 10Y rose 5bp but the KTB 10Y fell 2bp, so the whole move was local, and over four weeks the KTB's −11.6bp splits into +11.8bp from Treasuries (weekly beta 0.62, US 10Y +19bp) and −23.4bp of Korea's own rally.

The local drivers still favour bonds: KOSPI is back at 5,100, foreigners are selling stock and buying futures, broker deposits are down KRW 7tn in four weeks and the rotation signal reads bond rally (weekly +1.08, daily +1.47), though the weekly reading has eased from +1.62 four weeks ago.

Against that, the front end is pinned by a priced November 26 hike (1Y at the 90th percentile, bills at 1-year highs), so the rally runs through the long end rather than a bull steepening; I expect the 10Y in a 3.90–4.08% range into the BOK.
I keep the 10Y long (average 3.975%, now 0.6bp against) and stay flat 3s10s, since KOSPI did not hold 5,300.

Hedged remains the better way to hold it: against 0.5 × US 10Y the long is about +5bp, and the signal's hedged record (rally calls right 68%, sell-off calls 69%, Sharpe 1.35, worst drawdown −26bp) beats outright (52%, 57%, 0.91, −36bp); Nvidia results on Tuesday night and FOMC minutes on Wednesday are the main risks.

buckets.name: KTB 1–2Y front end
buckets.why: The 2Y fell 0.8bp to 3.741%, 84th percentile of its 1-year range (average 3.39%), while the 1Y was flat at 3.633% (90th). 2s3s is 0.2bp (2nd percentile, average 13bp) and 1s2s 10.8bp (4th). MSB 91-day (3.206%), CD (3.38%) and CP (3.84%) are all at 1-year highs and price a November 26 hike to 3.25%, so the front end did not join the rally.
buckets.call: Keep: buy the 2Y above 3.80%, target 3.65%, stop 3.90%. Not triggered (6bp away).

buckets.name: 3s10s curve
buckets.why: 3s10s flattened 0.4bp to 23.8bp (2nd percentile, average 40bp, 1-year low 20.8bp) as the long end led the rally. The 3s5s10s fly is −6.4bp (2nd percentile, average 4.3bp), so the 5Y stays the richest point. Our earlier steepener was stopped on Nov 5.
buckets.call: Stay flat: KOSPI traded above 5,300 only at the open and closed at 5,100, so the re-entry trigger was not met. Re-enter the steepener (3 × 3Y vs 1 × 10Y futures, DV01 about KRW 86k each side) only on a KOSPI close above 5,300 or after a BOK hike; target 32bp, stop 19bp.

buckets.name: KTB 10Y outright
buckets.why: The 10Y at 3.981% is at the 51st percentile of a 3.25–4.60% range (average 3.92%). The long from 3.95% and 4.00% averages about 3.975%, 0.6bp against outright. Today Treasuries implied +2.4bp and the 10Y fell 2bp, so against 0.5 × US 10Y the hedged position is about +5bp since entry.
buckets.call: Long, average 3.975%, stop 4.10%, target 3.85%; hold against about 0.5 × US 10Y. Open, −0.6bp outright, about +5bp hedged.

buckets.name: Ultra-long 30–50Y
buckets.why: 30s50s held at −2.3bp (88th percentile, average −9.1bp) as the 30Y and 50Y fell 2.4bp and 2.2bp, so the switch from +2.5bp is 4.8bp in favour, 0.7bp from target. The 10s20s30s fly eased 1bp to 12.3bp (72nd) as the 20Y outperformed.
buckets.call: Keep the 30Y into 50Y switch from +2.5bp; target −3bp, stop +0.5bp. Open, +4.8bp.

buckets.name: KDB 1–3Y vs KTB
buckets.why: The KDB fit (24 trades) puts the 3Y 18.1bp over KTB, 4.9bp wider on the day as KDB paper lagged the rally, at the 42nd percentile (average 19.6bp). The 1Y fit is 29bp over (66th) and KOFIA's 1Y KDB quote 25.1bp (53rd). We took profit at 20bp on Nov 13; KEXIM has only 3 trades (low confidence).
buckets.call: Flat. Re-enter overweight only if the 3Y spread returns above 22bp; 4bp away.

buckets.name: AAA bank debentures and money market
buckets.why: AAA bank paper (35-trade fit) is 39.0bp over the 1Y KTB, 84th percentile (average 31bp), 0.6bp tighter; the 3Y is 28.6bp over (50th) after a 2.5bp tightening. CD rose 1bp to 3.38% with CP flat at 3.84%, so CP–CD is 46bp (91st, average 29bp) and CD–MSB91 17bp (29th). IBK 1Y (30 trades) is 31bp over, 72nd percentile.
buckets.call: No change: revisit bank paper once CP–CD falls below 35bp; prefer the 1Y over the 3Y if adding.

buckets.name: Corporate credit (AA- 3Y)
buckets.why: AA- 3Y fell 1.8bp to 4.416%, a touch more than the KTB 3Y, so the spread is 67.3bp (68th percentile, average 62bp). KEPCO 3Y is 40.8bp over (80th, average 35bp) and BBB- minus AA- 583bp (76th). Credit has not cheapened despite the equity slide.
buckets.call: Add AA- only above 75bp or once KOSPI regains 5,300; no trigger hit.

watch: Next: Fed Chair Warsh speaks (Nov 16, New York), US retail sales and Nvidia results (Nov 17), FOMC minutes (Nov 18), the college entrance exam on Nov 19 (KRX opens an hour late), Nov 1–20 exports around Nov 23, the BOK decision on Nov 26 (hike to 3.25% priced) and the FOMC on Dec 8–9; KTBs take about 0.45–0.5bp per Treasury bp on the day.
